title: Mannahanning / Coney Island
summary: A Coney Island name from Kings County, shown as a modern orientation point rather than an exact 1654 deed boundary.
map_geometry_source: Approximate modern Coney Island coordinate used for a general placename marker.
introduction_content: Mannahanning is a recorded name for Coney Island in Kings County. It appears alongside Narriock, a related name in a seventeenth-century release.
translation_content:
The name is interpreted Mannahanning as land on the island or island land. He contrasts it with Narriock, which he reads as a point of land.

Why Place Names Matter

“Place names are stories for places. They can be a tool for learning that encourages a deeper understanding of the unique histories of our places.”

— Northern Territory Place Names Committee, Engagement Framework: Place Naming in the Northern Territory (2022), opening place-names explanation

Place-name history should show Native people as active and present, not only as names in old documents.
whereintheworld_content: The map placement is placed on modern Coney Island to orient readers to the placename, not an exact boundary for the 1654 release or for the older island and neck landscape.
